details.intro:
The Testamentum protoplastorum (Testament of the First-Created / Protoplasts) is a lost primeval pseudepigraphon cited by the 7th-century Sinaitic monk and theologian Pseudo-Anastasius of Sinai in his In Hexaemeron, Book VII.

The text provided chronological and halakhic determinations concerning the first humans, stating the exact days of Adam's naming of the animals, his forty days in the wilderness prior to entering Paradise, and the timeline of the transgression and fall.

Scholarly Debate: Adolf von Harnack held that this title designated a distinct, lost Greek work of the Adam cycle. Conversely, M. R. James and Hermann Rönsch demonstrated that Pseudo-Anastasius' quotation closely matches the reckoning of primeval weeks in the Book of Jubilees (Jub 3:1–9), suggesting the title may represent a Greek patristic designation for the opening chapters of Jubilees.
details.provenance:
Language: Greek.
Date: 7th century CE citation reflecting early Hellenistic Jewish or Second Temple traditions.
Setting: Monastic patristic transmission citing non-canonical chronological authorities.
details.manuscripts:
• Patristic Witness: Pseudo-Anastasius Sinaita, In Hexaemeron, Book VII (CPG 7770; PG 89, col. 967D; ed. C. A. Sackur / Kuehn).
  • Comparative Witnesses: George Syncellus, Chronographia; Book of Jubilees 3:1–9.
